problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-2,5),(4,-3),(3,2).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{{180}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${180}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(2,5)$
- $(-4,-3)$
- $(-3,-2)$
worked_solution:
The counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{{180}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${180}^{∘}$ is given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{{180}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{{180}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & -3 \\ -5 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(2,-5),(-4,3),(-3,-2).$

So, the correct answer is "III only."
